title: Info Session: ANSC 398 - Animal Exploration in Sri Lanka
description: Come learn more about the NEW Animal Explorations in Sri Lanka program running in May 2027! Sri Lanka is home to an extraordinary variety of wildlife, including Asian elephants, leopards, primates, sea turtles, marine mammals, peacocks, ornamental fish, and pollinators such as honey bees. Students will travel across the country to observe these animals in their natural habitats, visit research and conservation facilities, engage with veterinary and wildlife professionals, and explore how cultural traditions influence animal welfare and conservation policies. The program combines classroom learning with experiential education, allowing students to connect scientific concepts with real-world conservation challenges and solutions. title: Women of Valor Exhibit Opening
location: Illinois History and Lincoln Collections\, 324 Main Library\, 1408 W. Gregory Drive\, Urbana
description: Please join us for the opening of the Illinois History and Lincoln Collection's exhibit, Women of Valor: Creating Sisterhoods in Central Illinois. Jewish women in Central Illinois have been organizing for centuries. After uniting under the organizing arm of the National Federation of Temple Sisterhoods in 1920s, these women ushered in a century of community building and activism. The exhibit showcases the ways these women shaped their communities through the stories from three different Central Illinois cities. Join us to view the exhibit and highlights from the collections.  Refreshments and exhibit-themed coloring pages will be provided.

title: IMMERSE Seminar - Shenlong Wang: May the Force Be with Your Pixels
location: Siebel School of Computing and Data Science Room 2405
description: This event is hybrid, in person at 2405 Siebel Center for Computer Science and on Zoom via: https://go.illinois.edu/immerseseminarwangAbstract: One long-term goal of my group’s research is to understand and simulate the physical world from visual observations, to support what-if prediction under actions and forces. In this talk, I will present our recent works on physical world models that connect pixels to explicit 3D state and dynamics, and integrate physical simulation with generative models to create interactive, physically grounded visual experiences. I will highlight applications in robotics and agriculture, and conclude with open directions toward making all images and videos interactive at scale.  Speaker Bio: Shenlong Wang is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He works on computer vision and robotics, with a focus on understanding, modeling, and simulating the physical world for content creation, robotics, and AI for science. His work has received paper awards and finalist recognitions at ISMAR, IROS, and CVPR, and he is a recipient of the NSF CAREER Award. Refreshments will be provided.

title: Student Coffee Talk with Austin Strange
description: The Center for East Asian & Pacific Studies would like to invite interested students to a discussion & coffee, with Professor Austin Strange in connection to his talk titled, \"Is Soft Power a Zero-Sum Competition?\" Coffee and treats will be provided. Biography: Austin Strange is an Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Politics and Public Administration at the University of Hong Kong, where he directs the Master of International and Public Affairs (MIPA) program. He researches and teaches international relations, international development, and Chinese foreign policy. He is the author of Chinese Global Infrastructure (Cambridge University Press) and co-author of Banking on Beijing: The Aims and Impacts of China’s Overseas Development Program (Cambridge University Press). At HKU he received the Early Career Teaching Award in 2022, Research Output Prize in 2023, and Outstanding Young Researcher Award in 2024. With colleagues Austin was awarded the Best New Dataset Award from the International Political Economy Society for developing AidData's Global Chinese Development Finance Dataset. Austin earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, an M.A. from Zhejiang University, and a B.A. from College of William and Mary.

title: Future of Work Symposium: Industry-Academy Insights on the Future of AI at Work
location: I Hotel & Illinois Conference Center\; Alma Mater Room
description: _ About the Symposium The 4th Future of Work Symposium brings together industry leaders and University of Illinois researchers to explore how organizations can promote and facilitate the constructive use of artificial intelligence in the workplace. Through dialogue between those developing and implementing AI tools in industry and those studying their social and behavioral implications, the symposium will examine how AI is reshaping organizations, work, and the employee experience.  The 2026 symposium builds on three previous events (October 2022, April 2023, and November 2024) that brought together researchers and practitioners to explore the future of work._ Featured Industry Leaders The symposium will feature insights from leaders working across recruiting analytics, productivity research, organizational communication, and AI-enabled workplace technologies:Dr. Mengyang Cao, Head of Recruiting Analytics at Anthropic. Cao previously spent nearly a decade on Meta’s People Analytics team and holds a PhD in Industrial-Organizational Psychology from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.  Dr. Shamsi Iqbal, Principal Applied and Data Science Manager at Microsoft. Iqbal focuses on productivity research and data- and research-backed approaches to helping organizations and people thrive in the changing workplace. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.  Dr. Katie Kang, Organizational Scientist and faculty member at George Washington University. Kang brings expertise in organizational communication, ethnographic research, and digital transformation, with experience spanning academic and industry roles. _ What to ExpectCheck-in & Light Breakfast | 8:30–9:00 a.m. Arrive early to check in and enjoy a light breakfast before the symposium begins. Research Agenda-Setting Workshop | 9:00–11:45 a.m. Industry leaders will share concrete use cases from their work, followed by facilitated discussion connecting real-world practices with potential directions for research. The session will conclude with reflections from the industry leaders. Additional Sessions: Building Effective Industry-Academy Partnerships | 12:00–2:00 p.m. Faculty and industry leaders will discuss models for developing partnerships focused on AI and the societal transformations associated with its use. Special Graduate Student Session | 2:15–3:15 p.m. Doctoral students are invited to an additional session focused on careers at the intersection of academia and industry. Students will have an opportunity to learn from and engage with the symposium speakers._ Continuing the Conversation This year's symposium is jointly hosted by the Social & Behavioral Science Institute, School of Labor and Employment Relations, and the Siebel School of Computing and Data Science. By bringing academic and industry perspectives together, the event aims to foster discussion about the future of AI at work and lay the groundwork for lasting industry-academy connections.

title: Overcoming Barriers Towards the Catalytic Deconstruction and Upgrading of  Plastic Waste
description: Single-use plastics such as polyolefins provide effective packaging and materials for food, medicine, and many other consumer products, which has led to massive global generation of plastic waste. This waste is accumulating in landfills and the environment, causing harm to the ecosystem and human health. While a small fraction of plastic waste is mechanically recycled, the material quality cannot yet compete with virgin polymers. Chemical recycling with heterogeneous catalysis offers an opportunity to reduce the energy required to selectively deconstruct polyolefins into higher value fuels, chemicals, and monomers. Hydrogenolysis and hydrocracking are emerging methods of lowering the energy required to break the strong bonds in polymers through the use of a catalyst and hydrogen gas\; however, the scalability of these technologies is limited by the high cost of reactants, the requirement for high pressure molecular hydrogen or solvents, and the high cost of catalytic materials. This talk will start by discussing advances in the catalytic depolymerization of waste plastics with earth-abundant catalysts, followed by progress in hydrogen-free depolymerization pathways. The talk will close with a discussion on emerging frameworks for the chemical recycling of mixed plastic waste feedstocks and an outlook on remaining technical challenges as well as economic and environmental considerations in polymer upcycling, redesign, and circularity. Dr. Julie E. Rorrer is an Assistant Professor of Chemical Engineering at the University of Washington, Seattle. Her research group focuses on using heterogeneous catalysis for the chemical recycling of waste plastics and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals.  She received her PhD in Chemical Engineering from UC Berkeley and her BS from Arizona State University. Prior to UW, she was a Beckman Postdoctoral fellow at MIT. Her recent awards include the ARPA-E IGNIITE Award, and the American Institute of Chemical Engineers 35 Under 35 Award. In addition to her work in catalysis, she is the founder of the ongoing educational initiative, ColorMePhD, which creates free coloring activities to explain current research in STEM to aspiring scientists and engineers.
